svg.title: Software criticality · Table V (SwCI) and LOR worksheet
svg.desc: Spreadsheet view of Software criticality · Table V (SwCI) and LOR, generated from safety/software/SSF-*.yaml + hazard records.
svg.text: Software criticality · Table V (SwCI) and LOR — worksheet
swci-assessment.csv · generated from safety/software/SSF-*.yaml + hazard records
8 rows · SwCI = Table V (SCC x worst severity of the hazards that reference the function). It is not a risk assessment (4.4.2).

g.text: Terms: AI = artificial intelligence (here, an AI assistant drafting at independence level I0) · DoD = US Department of Defense · F-nnn = system function in the item definition · HAZ-nnn = hazard record (safety/hazards/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml) ·

I0–I3 = review independence level (I0 none, e.g. the author or an AI, to I3 independent organisation) · LOR = level of rigor (software safety tasks, MIL-STD-882E 4.4) · MIL-STD-882E = US DoD Standard Practice for System Safety (11 May

2012, base edition) · PX4 = PX4 Autopilot, the open-source flight-control software candidate for SUS-A1 · SCC = software control category (MIL-STD-882E Table IV) · SSF-nnn = safety-significant software function record (safety/software/) ·

SUS-A1 = dockable observation UAV · SwCI = software criticality index (MIL-STD-882E Table V) · SYS-nnn = system safety requirement record (requirements/SYS-nnn.yaml) · SysML = Systems Modeling Language (SysML v2) · UAV = uncrewed aerial
vehicle (drone) · US = United States · V-nnn = SysML view (tools/sysml/views.py)
